domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers
q is treated as a formal indeterminate, not a specialized numeric value
n is a nonnegative integer in the q-Pochhammer definition
The product for (q;q)_0 is the empty product and equals 1
D is nonnegative because r is nonnegative and b minus a is nonnegative
The identity is an equality of rational functions over the integers, not a pointwise analytic statement
In the polynomial conclusion, R_{a,b,r}(q) is assumed to simplify to an element of the integer polynomial ring
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For any integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, the rational function R_{a,b,r}(q) is self-reciprocal of degree D = r times (b minus a), meaning q to the power D times R_{a,b,r} at q inverse equals R_{a,b,r}(q) in the rational function field over the integers. If this rational function is in fact an integer polynomial, then its coefficients can be indexed from 0 to D so that the coefficient list is palindromic: c_j equals c_{D-j} for every j.
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r satisfying 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
For all nonnegative integers n, define the q-Pochhammer symbol by the finite product over j from 1 to n, with the n = 0 case equal to 1
Define R_{a,b,r}(q) from these factors and define D as r times (b minus a)
The identity q to the power D times R_{a,b,r} evaluated at q inverse equals R_{a,b,r}(q) holds in the rational function field over the integers

If R_{a,b,r}(q) lies in the polynomial ring over the integers, then there exist integers c_0 through c_D such that R_{a,b,r}(q) equals the sum of c_j q^j from j = 0 to D and the coefficients satisfy c_j = c_{D-j} for every j from 0 to D

witness_dependencies: The polynomial coefficients c_0 through c_D, when they exist, depend on the fixed parameters a, b, and r through the polynomial R_{a,b,r}(q)
The symmetry relation c_j = c_{D-j} uses the same coefficient list c_0 through c_D; there is no separate witness for each j
The integer D is determined uniquely by a, b, and r as r times (b minus a)

statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Then the rational-function identity q^D R_{a,b,r}(q^(-1)) = R_{a,b,r}(q) holds in Z(q). Consequently, whenever R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], there exist integers c_0, ..., c_D such that R_{a,b,r}(q) = sum_{j=0}^D c_j q^j and c_j = c_{D-j} for every j with 0 <= j <= D.
